1.explanation:
1) lib/features/auto-place/AutoPlace.js – this is where the append operation is triggered. It calls modeling.connect to wire the new task to the old one and therefore is where the illegal mid-segment (and its waypoints array) first shows up.

2) lib/features/modeling/BpmnUpdater.js – the updater hook that listens for new connections ends up copying the connection’s diagram waypoints onto the SequenceFlow businessObject, instead of routing them into a proper BPMNEdge DI element.

3) lib/util/DiUtil.js – serializes DI information. Because the SequenceFlow businessObject now carries a raw `waypoints` property, moddle dutifully writes it out as an XML attribute. The fix is to strip `waypoints` off the BPMN element (or never attach it) and only emit the bend points inside `<bpmndi:BPMNEdge><di:waypoint…/>` elements.
1.bug_scenario: A new task is appended to an existing task via the “+” auto-place handle, and because the two tasks sit at different vertical positions the connecting sequenceFlow acquires a middle bend. Under the hood Diagram-JS tracks that bend in a `waypoints` array on the connection graphic, but the BPMN updater code mistakes that for a business-object property and pushes it onto the SequenceFlow element itself. When the XML is written out, moddle sees this unknown `waypoints` field on the SequenceFlow BPMN element and serializes it as an attribute — yielding the invalid `waypoints="[object Object],[object Object],…"` on `<sequenceFlow>` instead of proper DI waypoints in a `<bpmndi:BPMNEdge>`.

2.explanation:
• AppendBehavior.js: this behavior wires up the “append” handle and ultimately calls into the connection creation routine when you drag out a new task. It is the entry point for the faulty flow.  

• Modeling.js: defines the connect/createConnection command – it’s where the connection’s businessObject is instantiated and where any extra properties (including an errant `waypoints` prop) may end up on the sequenceFlow.  

• BpmnLayouter.js: computes the actual bend points for multi-segment flows. It hands back an array of point objects, but those are only supposed to be used when writing the DI, not grafted onto the businessObject.  

• DiUtil.js: responsible for creating/updating the BPMN DI edge (<bpmndi:BPMNEdge>) and serializing <di:waypoint> children. This is where the computed waypoints should go. Because the modeler has also attached waypoints to the businessObject, moddle serializes them as an illegal attribute.  

• ReplaceConnectionBehavior.js: in certain repointing scenarios (e.g. reconnect or replace), existing connections get cloned and waypoints get copied verbatim – again onto the businessObject rather than solely into the DI.  

In short, these modules jointly compute and propagate waypoint data. Right now they accidentally stash that data on the SequenceFlow model (so moddle renders it as an invalid `waypoints` attribute) instead of only on the BPMN DI edge. Fixing this requires stripping or preventing the `waypoints` property on the businessObject and pushing it exclusively into the DI via DiUtil.
2.bug_scenario:
When you use the little “+” handle on an existing task to append a new task, the modeler computes a bent connection (i.e. a sequenceFlow with a middle segment) and ends up writing a non-standard waypoints attribute onto the bpmn:SequenceFlow itself. In the exported XML you see this:

  <sequenceFlow id="..." sourceRef="..." targetRef="..." waypoints="[object Object],[object Object],[object Object],[object Object]"/>

Those waypoint objects belong in the BPMN DI (bpmndi:BPMNEdge) as <di:waypoint> children – not on the business object. The result is invalid XML.
